findings.anchor: tests/unit/instruction-diet-revert.bats:@test "IDR-3 the twelve constraint rationales carry their pre-diet text"
findings.description: The new regression tests expect `.claude/data/constraints.json` to contain objects with `id` and `why` fields, but the same diff adds that file as a flat `{id: rationale}` map. The recursive walker in IDR-3 never records any entries, and IDR-4's jq selector `select(.id? == $id) | .why` returns null for every C-PROC row.
findings.failure_mode: The newly added Bats suite fails deterministically: IDR-3 reports every expected rationale as mismatched, and IDR-4 greps for `| null |` in `CLAUDE.loa.md`. This makes CI red immediately after the change.
findings.suggested_fix: Either restore `constraints.json` to the schema the tests and renderers expect, with objects carrying `id` and `why`, or update IDR-3 and IDR-4 to read the new flat mapping shape, e.g. `found = json.load(...)` and `jq -r --arg id "$id" '.[$id]'`.

findings.description: The constraints.json hunk in this diff renders the file as a flat {"C-PROC-001": "<why>", ...} map. Both new tests that read it assume a different shape: IDR-3's Python walk only records entries from dicts that carry both an `id` and a `why` key, and IDR-4's jq filter is `[.. | objects | select(.id? == $id) | .why][0]`. Against a flat map neither finds anything. The hunk header is `@@ -0,0 +1,14 @@` against a non-empty preimage blob (795a23bd is not the empty blob), so the hunk is almost certainly a synthesized rendering rather than real git output, but the inconsistency between the data as shown and the readers as written needs to be confirmed against the actual file.
findings.failure_mode: If .claude/data/constraints.json really is a flat id-to-string map: IDR-3 leaves `found` empty, all 12 ids land in `bad`, and the test exits 1. IDR-4's jq prints `null` for every id and `grep -qF "| null |"` fails on all seven rows. The sprint report's claim that IDR-1–4 went red-then-green would then be false.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the committed constraints.json carries `{id, why}` objects (nested under whatever tier/list structure the renderer expects). If it does, no change; if the file was flattened, restore the object shape or rewrite IDR-3/IDR-4 to read the flat map (`.[$id]`).

findings.description: IDR-3 hard-depends on `tests/fixtures/constraint-rationales-pre-diet.json` (must exist, must parse, must contain exactly 12 keys), but that fixture is not part of this diff. If it was not already committed in Sprint 3, `json.load(open(sys.argv[2]))` raises FileNotFoundError and the test fails for a reason unrelated to the rationales. The fixture also becomes a third copy of the same 12 strings (constraints.json, the two golden tables, and this file), so any future wording edit must be made in three places or IDR-3/IDR-4 go red.
findings.failure_mode: Test fails with a Python traceback instead of a mismatch list when the fixture is absent; later rationale edits silently fall out of sync across the three copies and the revert guard fails on wording rather than on the intended regression.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add the fixture in this change set (and reference it in the report), or derive the expected text from the golden tables already pinned under tests/fixtures/ so there is one source of truth for the rendered rationale strings.

findings.description: LOA_LIMIT goes 9,216 B back to 10,240 B. The report discloses that the Sprint 3 acceptance criterion "CLAUDE.loa.md ≤ 9,216 B" is being given up under the pre-registered A/B rule, which is a legitimate outcome, but the budget constant is the only place the diff touches. The current CLAUDE.loa.md is reported at 10,225 B, leaving 15 bytes of headroom, so the next one-word edit to that file will fail CI. Any remaining references to the 9,216 figure (sprint plan AC text, CHANGELOG, README, CI sentinel fixture trees used via `--root`) are now stale and will contradict the tool.
findings.failure_mode: Requirements-traceability checks that read the Sprint 3 AC text still see an unmet AC; a stale sentinel fixture sized to the 9,216 limit stops exercising the breach path; the first non-trivial CLAUDE.loa.md change after merge breaks the budget gate with no slack to absorb it.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the Sprint 3 AC / sprint plan to record the reverted budget and cite the A/B rule, grep the tree for `9216` and `9,216` and update or remove the stale references, and consider whether 10,240 B should be re-derived from the measured pre-diet size plus explicit headroom rather than restored as a bare constant.
